thread:
alice: FYI customer reported a hard p99 latency spike on their Dedicated pool around 09:12 UTC. They saw p99 jump to ~6s (normally ~0.9s). Happening during a traffic surge, errors not present but requests queueing. Escalating to SRE. :warning:
ana: ack. which pool / pool id? any request ids from their side?
mike: looking at metrics now — CPU/GPU util on that pool hit 98% for 60s, queue length climbed. Autoscaler shows scale event but it took ~2m for new nodes to register. Cold GPU initialization adds ~45s.
kevin: I'm pulling autoscaler logs. Early sign: several scale_up attempts back-to-back then a throttle in our controller because of concurrent scale ops. Possibly hitting cloud API rate limits.
indra: can you paste the autoscaler log snippet? also what model size are they running? big LLMs can have longer warmup.
alice: they say model is rdlm-13b-quant (our dedicated variant). They provided sample request ids: req_8352, req_8359. No 500s. Just long tail responses.
mike: log excerpt: ```
[autoscaler] 09:11:58 scale_up pool=d-pool-17 desired=4->6 reason=util>0.85
[autoscaler] 09:12:03 cloud-api rate_limit=429 delay=7s
[autoscaler] 09:13:00 scale_up failed: instance-init-timeout
[serving] 09:13:50 gpu-warmup start, kv-cache miss
[serving] 09:14:35 gpu-ready host=10.4.22.7
```
josh: so timeline: desired went up quickly but cloud and instance init added ~2 minutes, plus model warmup ~45s. That explains the p99.
a na: reproduce steps I suggest: run a controlled ramp test to hit 90% util on a dedicated pool and observe scale path + p99. We should measure two things separately: 1) autoscaler controller latency (kube->cloud) 2) model warmup time on cold GPU image.
kevin: reproduced locally in staging. Autoscaler cooldown is 30s, but cloud API backoff set to exponential with jitter — when we hit concurrent scale ops, the throttle pushes things out to 90-120s in worst-case. Also noticed image pull for runtime container sometimes waits on registry auth.
indra: interesting — runtime image size is 2.1GB plus model artifact pull (if not pre-cached) which is ~1.8GB for quantized 13b. If instance boots with empty local cache it has to fetch weights. That explains the big chunk of time.
mike: mitigation options: 1) bump min replicas for this pool to reduce cold starts 2) enable pre-warming for bursty customers (keep 1 warm standby) 3) improve autoscaler concurrency with batch scale operations 4) use a smaller fallback model during scale-up 5) tune cloud API rate limits / use higher quota.
alice: customer is asking for immediate mitigation — can we do a short-term config change?
kevin: we can set pool min=4 for that customer's pool (currently 2) and enable prewarm flag. I can do a temporary change and monitor. Any objections?
indra: +1 for quick fix. Also we should push a follow-up ticket to improve image caching (keep weights on ephemeral SSD snapshot) and to reduce model pull time.
josh: I'll coordinate the rollout. Plan: 1) kevin updates pool min and enables prewarm 2) mike runs load ramp to validate p99 improvements 3) monitor for 30m then rollback if cost/side-effects.
nana: please also add an incident tag to this thread and notify support-replay once mitigation is in.
kevin: executing now: `redwoodctl dedicated update --pool d-pool-17 --min-replicas 4 --prewarm=true` — deploy-bot: started operation op-9876.
deploy-bot: operation op-9876 accepted, estimated completion 90s.
sre-bot: alert muted for d-pool-17 autoscale flapping for 1h (temporary).
(about 7m later)
mike: post-change quick metrics: new min=4 active by 09:20, average queue length dropped, p99 back to ~1.1s for the customer's traffic window. CPU/GPU util reduced to ~62%. Early looks good. :thumbsup:
ale x: cost note — bumping min has cost impact, but temporary. Please file cost-authorize for customer workaround.
alice: customer notified, they reported initial improvement. We're calling this "hotfix" while we work on longer-term improvements.
indra: long-term action items: - implement model artifact pre-seeding on node image - add a warm standby pool config to maintain N warm replicas - improve autoscaler to coalesce scale up requests and increase concurrency quota - add a fallback model route in the runtime router so requests can hit a smaller model during warmups
mike: I'll open a GH issue with diagnostics and attach the graphs/logs + repro steps. Tagging infra and runtime teams.
kevin: opened infra/issue #4321 "d-pool-17 scale-up lag + cold start mitigation" with logs and proposed remediation.
josh: next steps: follow-up postmortem in #postmortems after we collect full metrics. For now hotfix worked, leaving monitoring on for 2 hours.
alice: thanks all — closing the customer loop now. If anyone sees regressions re-open thread. :white_check_mark:
